title: Grateful Dead Live at The Silver Dollar Fair on 1968-11-01
lineage: SBD > MR > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a fiery 1968 set with stellar Dark Star, The Other One and Feedback, but marred by severe tape drop‑outs in the middle.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its raw intensity – dark, trippy passages like Dark Star, Cryptical Envelopment, Feedback and an almost legendary take on The Other One shine through.  The board mix initially puts Jerry’s amp‑driven tone front‑and‑center, but the recording collapses after New Potato, with muffled drums and long drop‑outs that make large sections unlistenable.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4–5 stars for its musical fire, but many flag serious recording defects that pull the overall experience down to a mid‑high range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early part of the tape is crisp with Jerry prominently in the mix, but after New Potato the sound deteriorates sharply – drop‑outs, muffled drums and overall “unlistenable” sections dominate the middle of the set.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A powerful opening and intense middle (Dark Star, The Other One) give way to a fragmented listening experience because of the tape loss; the surviving tracks flow well but the gaps disrupt continuity.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his front‑center tone, fanned intro and “tube amp harmonics” that shine when the recording is clear.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass work is highlighted as brilliant interplay with Garcia on The Other One, described as “off‑the‑charts brilliant”.
band_member_comments.Keys: Reference to “Bear’s genius” in the mix; no specific comment about individual keyboard performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: A long drum solo is noted but suffers from poor tape quality and muffling.
